page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with 8 vCPUs, operating at 1.0 thread per core. The memory configuration consists of 32.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, and it operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.sn2.xlarge generally performs in the lower tiers for most compute and memory tasks. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng benchmarks falls into the bottom 25%, while single-core Geekbench scores are in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth read-only tests for both small and large blocks are also in the bottom 25%, though large block write operations achieve average performance. Compression and decompression tasks show poor to weak results, with single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scoring in the bottom 10%.

For specialized workloads, the instance demonstrates average performance in Passmark CPU scores and extended instruction tests. Small-scale language model inference using a 135M model also registers average speeds for both prompt processing and text generation, though scaling to a 7B model results in poor text generation speeds. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput consistently rank in the bottom 25%. Given the dedicated CPU allocation but lower benchmark performance relative to modern hardware, this instance is suited for general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, and lightweight application hosting that require dedicated CPU resources but do not demand high computational throughput.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2.xlarge is a general-purpose x86_64 server instance featuring 8 dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz and 32.0 GB of RAM. It operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps and contains no local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate that the instance generally operates in the lower tiers, with stress-ng CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores ranking in the bottom 25% and 10% respectively. However, it maintains average performance in Passmark CPU scores and small-scale LLM inference tasks. With a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance is suitable for general-purpose workloads, lightweight application hosting, and basic web serving where dedicated CPU allocation is required but extreme computational or memory throughput is not critical.
